notes: Summary: Orbiton Reserve is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a low-latency, high-throughput chat + personalization service used by trading desk clients.
Traffic profile: steady baseline 70k concurrent users, expect 40k active concurrent chat sessions during US market hours. Peak bursts during earnings windows (short spikes ~5-15 minutes).
Customer ask (core): Minimum sustained throughput guarantee and clear burst policy. Wants a contract line item: min tokens/sec across reserved pool + defined burst buffer with pricing caps.

Quant targets discussed on 2026-02-18 call: target sustained output >= 10,000 tokens/sec (aggregate) with p95 token completion latency < 200ms for 1k-token responses; concurrency cap ~120 active generation streams per model shard (customer micro-batching design).

Redwood proposal (initial): Reserved baseline equivalent to 8x H100-80GB (dedicated pool) delivering ~11k tokens/sec sustained with autoscaling headroom to borrow up to 3x shared burst nodes for short windows (billing: reserved baseline + metered burst at 1.5x rate).

Orbiton counter: Wants guaranteed hard burst capacity (not best-effort) for up to 10 minutes at 5x baseline without premium pricing >2x baseline. Concerned about tail latency under heavy KV cache misses and long-context requests.

SLA mechanics under discussion: define tokens/sec measured at model output stage (post-aggregation), specify measurement window (1m rolling), define credits for under-delivery (service credits or compute rollback).

Implementation items raised by SE: need clarifying the token-counting method (differences between client tokens, decoded tokens, and Redwood's internal byte/token mapping). Also must align on concurrency semantics: per-VM concurrency caps vs global per-customer concurrency cap.

Security/regulatory notes: Finance/legal require data residency in us-east-1 and strict audit logging for request/response metadata; Orbiton wants proof-of-concept in VPC/private deployment with KMS-managed keys.
Quote from CTO (call 2026-02-18): 'We cannot tolerate silent throttles during market events — burst guarantees are non-negotiable, but we need predictable billing.'

POC ask: 72-hour soak with synthetic and replayed production traces including KV cache cold-starts, runbook for failover to smaller model variants (fallback) and post-test perf report including tokens/sec, concurrency graphs, and cost per 1k tokens at baseline vs burst.

Legal/Procurement: initial term 12 months, negotiation on break/flex clauses for committed GPUs in year 1. Orbiton pushing for 30-day exit on non-performance; Redwood prefers graduated service credits and 90-day notice.
